analysis.answer: Current law requires a person to complete an eight-hour safety course and obtain a permit from the county sheriff to carry a concealed handgun. The measure eliminates the safety course and permit requirements for in-state concealed carry, while maintaining an optional permit system for out-of-state use.

Individuals will save the financial cost and time associated with taking an eight-hour safety course. Sheriffs' offices will likely see a reduction in administrative processing costs, as well as a corresponding drop in any fee revenue from in-state permit applications.

Removing the training and permit barrier will likely increase the number of people carrying concealed handguns. Some handgun owners will still apply for and renew permits to maintain reciprocity when traveling to other states.
The text addresses the regulatory burden on carrying a concealed handgun by entirely removing the permit and training requirements for adults who can lawfully possess one.

Individuals gain the discretion to carry concealed handguns without prior agency approval. The county sheriff loses the authority to verify training and issue permits as a prerequisite for in-state concealed carry.

The effect of permitless concealed carry on public safety is disputed. Some researchers find that removing permit and training requirements leads to increases in violent crime and firearm thefts, while others find no statistically significant impact on crime rates or argue it allows individuals to defend themselves more readily.
